answer: A concrete defense is per-identity staking gated by proof-of-work: every new agent must lock a fixed deposit and solve a rate-limited puzzle before it can transact, so mass registration costs real capital and time. Anchoring each identity to a hardware root of trust, like sealing a ledger into basalt, lets the network verify uniqueness through an atlas of attested devices, while a jetty-style queue throttles onboarding so bursts of clones queue behind a slow, observable ramp. An attacker cost scales linearly with the sybils they need.
